startupFollowup.interpretation: None of the installed startup/selection rejection edges recorded an event. This does not prove that every possible selection failure or exception was excluded. The exact history call was not labeled in this run.

diagnosticChanges: Opt-in BREDITOR_QUEUE_DELIVERY=1 augments the queue-only configuration with nine existing failed-delivery result edges and the terminal toolbarDispatchFailed call.

The toolbar probe records only closed delivery/submission/sequence/outcome/command/history tags, using own data properties and never invoking accessors or retaining identifiers, text, snapshots or errors.
The queue recorder remains responsible for original caught exceptions. Only browser_editor and command_queue are transformed; Wasm adapters and validators are untouched.
Formatted clipboard history now identifies each of its six Undo/Redo steps separately.

deliverySites.865: completed submission but lease not released while owner live
deliverySites.878: no admitted completion or recognized terminal result
deliverySites.932: terminal toolbar fault, with closed result tags

deliveryCatch.note: Both queue exception and owner delivery probes were active. Five boundary modules remained byte-identical. No captured reproduction.

deliveryStop.note: Queue execution loops and catch bodies were unchanged. Three independent failures were permitted before stopping the batch; no assertions or per-test timeouts were relaxed. No captured reproduction.

deliberateFailureControl.note: A separate control intentionally detaches its own temporary editor host, invokes a declared intent, and requires the original failed result plus exactly the first delivery breadcrumb. This proves recording works for that known failure; it does not reproduce the intermittent defect. The first control attempt used the wrong profile format version and failed startup in Chromium; correcting the fixture to match the existing v1 Highlight profile produced this passing run. Ordinary 54-case suite ordering is unchanged.

limitations: Cold-path recording can still affect compilation, inlining and timing. It is not optimization-neutral.
No production source, validation, recovery policy, Rust code, Wasm ABI, retry setting or test timeout changed.
An empty recorder excludes only its successfully observed edges; it does not establish a root cause or close earlier failures.
